name: NuDB
tagline: Header-only C++11 append-only key-value store tuned for random reads on SSDs, built for the XRP Ledger.
description: NuDB is an insert-only key-value store packaged as a header-only C++11 library, designed by Vinnie Falco (also the author of Boost.Beast) for content-addressable data where the key is a cryptographic digest. It keeps a data file and a separate key file of fixed-size hash buckets, so a lookup costs roughly one SSD read regardless of database size, memory use stays low, inserts are atomic, and the key file can be rebuilt from the data file; there are no updates or deletes, and all keys share one size. It was written for rippled, the XRP Ledger server, which runs it in production as a node-store backend. The code now lives under the C++ Alliance and receives occasional maintenance releases such as 2.0.9 in April 2025.
statusNote: Feature-complete; the C++ Alliance repository gets occasional fixes (2.0.9, April 2025).

scale.notes: File format supports databases up to 281 TB; read cost is designed to be independent of size.

strengths: About one SSD read per lookup no matter how large the database grows
Header-only with no separate library to build
Proven in production in the XRP Ledger's rippled server
weaknesses: All keys must be the same size
Only point lookups and full iteration; no range queries
